inherited_defect.what: tools/condense/glm52_external_baselines.py (534 lines) was deleted in 791ced2c as one of twelve campaign controllers retired with a specification, fixture, receipt and reopen condition. The retirement is recorded in tools/condense/engine/campaign_specs.json and engine/fixtures/retirement_receipts.json. But tools/condense/glm52_terminal_proofs.py still opens that path as evidence, and 21 tests error on its absence.
inherited_defect.significance: The retirement was procedurally complete and still left a live consumer pointing at a deleted file. This is the third instance in this repository's history of a reduction reported as capability-preserving while a real consumer broke -- after verify_grades.py and the HIDE concatenation. It is the reason control/REBUILD_ACCOUNTING_RULES.json makes the inventory --gate non-skippable and makes a check that stops running a red gate rather than a neutral one.
inherited_defect.disposition: Recorded as a baseline defect, not attributed to this campaign. The Behaviour Constitution must decide whether terminal-proof verification against external baselines is a protected observable behaviour; if it is, the rebuild owes it a working implementation, and if it is not, the 21 tests and their consumer are deletion candidates.

the_at_floor_seal.why: Every refusal behind that seal rests on something this campaign declassifies: public crate API, self-tested product schemas, code protected despite zero callers, cfg(test) surface, a host-selected A/B tuning lattice, and a crate manifest boundary. None of them is an observable behaviour.

what_remains_valid_as_evidence.reading: Deleting every named protection stops the CURRENT architecture at 349,455. That measures how much of the current tree is load-bearing for the current architecture. It is not a bound on a different one.
